notes.10: Candidates failed to appreciate that it is by diffusion and not by osmosis that water moves through stomata.
notes.12: The question required knowledge on the action of a protease, and an understanding of the term ‘product’. One, the other or both of these requirements were not in evidence. Cambridge International General Certificate of Secondary Education 0610 Biology June 2010
notes.13: Candidates often fail accurately to learn the details surrounding the two vitamins named in the syllabus. Such was the case with this relatively straightforward question.
notes.15: Although slightly complicated at first sight, this question required knowledge of the function of phloem which candidates confused with that of xylem.
notes.19: This question became largely a matter of guesswork if the candidates’ knowledge of the difference in composition between inspired and expired air did not include any quantitative detail.
notes.32: Osmosis was already identified as a hazy area ( Question 10 ) but candidates showed consistency in believing that it is involved in water loss rather than in water uptake. Cambridge International General Certificate of Secondary Education 0610 Biology June 2010
